Braun T 1000 world receiver, 1963

Dieter Rams’s portable short-wave radio for Braun: an aluminium case with a perforated speaker panel, a dark tuning scale, and a front flap that holds the manual.

Source
Victoria and Albert Museum, W.12:1 to 3-2007
Creator
Dieter Rams, designer; Braun AG, manufacturer
Made
1963 (V&A date field); the V&A brief description says 1961
Style
Ulm School (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Precise, technical, rational
Evidence
Inspected the V&A’s primary image 2007BR3164 of object W.12:1 to 3-2007 at 1067 × 1600 px, through the V&A IIIF service.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A dates the object 1963 in its production fields, while its brief description says “West Germany, 1961”. It is an “oblong aluminium radio with drop down flap on the front, revealing dials and controls”, 24.5 × 36.2 × 13.4 cm. V&A W.12:1 to 3-2007.

The V&A notes that the complex wavebands needed “a thick user manual, stored in the drop-down cover”, and that the aerials and dials give it “the character of a piece of military or surveillance equipment”. V&A.

Observed

  • The case is matte silver aluminium with slightly rounded vertical edges and a black top strip with a bar handle.
  • A tall panel on the left is covered in very fine, regular perforation.
  • A black tuning scale fills the upper right with rows of small white numerals. Two large white knobs sit at its right edge, one with a red dot.
  • Below, five dark knobs, four toggle switches, and three round sockets line up in three rows. A column of four white round buttons ends in one orange button.
  • The open front flap holds the printed manual.

Why it belongs

The T 1000 shows that the style can carry dense controls. The density stays calm because every part sits on the same rows and columns and the color is held back.

Borrow

Use a finely perforated panel next to a dense control area to give the eye a rest.

Put many small controls on a strict grid, and give color to one button only.
